title: Repair pagination boundaries
instructions:
The existing pagination helper has exactly two arithmetic bugs. Fix them
while preserving its public API and the following behavior.

## Files
- `pagination.py`: repair `paginate(items, page=1, per_page=10, radius=1) -> dict`.

`items` is a finite iterable. page and per_page must be positive integers,
excluding bool; radius must be a nonnegative integer excluding bool. Any
invalid option raises ValueError. Materialize items once. Return a dictionary
with exactly these keys:
- `items`: a fresh list for the requested one-based page; [] beyond the end.
- `page`, `per_page`: the requested values, never clamped.
- `total`: item count; `pages`: ceiling(total/per_page), or 0 when empty.
- `has_previous`: total > 0 and page > 1.
- `has_next`: page < pages.
- `previous_page`: min(page-1, pages) if has_previous, otherwise None.
- `next_page`: page+1 if has_next, otherwise None.
- `window`: all valid page numbers from page-radius through page+radius
  inclusive, ascending; do not shift the window to compensate for edges.

Empty input has no navigation and an empty window for any requested page.
Mutating the returned items list must not mutate the input list. The helper
functions are internal and need not be tested or exposed separately.
